source.title: linear probes for space and time

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes selected space- and time-sensitive neurons, but does not measure neuron-pole job counts, explanation quality on held-out activations, the proposed InceptionV1 examples, or attribution-graph sufficiency.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron selectivity, a single-neuron intervention, and selected-neuron ablations. These findings concern particular space/time neurons, not the versions’ proposed audit shares or explanation tests. No rows are linked to a claim version. The paper also says features may be distributed in superposition, making individual neurons the wrong level of analysis; it does not test the claim’s numerical audit shares.
record.test_reason: The study probes Llama-2 and Pythia for linear space/time representations and examines a handful of hand-selected space/time neurons. It reports no share of interpretable neurons, no explanation-scoring on held-out text, no InceptionV1 analysis and no neuron-based attribution graphs. The neuron results concern particular neurons chosen by probe similarity, not an audit of neuron jobs, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Llama-2 models learn linear space and time representations that are unified across entity types and fairly robust to prompting. They add that individual 'space' and 'time' neurons exist and are causally relevant. They say the full structure of these representations is unclear and expect features to be distributed in superposition. The record omits that the representations were found to improve with model scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear probes to locate spatial and temporal directions, then searches for similar neurons and intervenes on selected neurons. It does not use the neuron-pole explanation audit or held-out explanation tests described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompting changes performance: random distracting tokens degrade probe performance, capitalization also degrades it, and probing the period after a headline improves it.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual MLP neurons in Llama-2 chosen for similarity to probe directions track space or time coordinates across entity types. Pinning or ablating them changes predictions or loss in selected contexts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some single neurons in Llama-2 encode continuous spatial or temporal coordinates and causally affect related predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state they 'generally expect features to be distributed in superposition', making individual neurons the wrong level of analysis. This is stated as an expectation, not tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Authors' prior that features are distributed in superposition rather than neuron-aligned (untested opinion).

record.problems: The neuron intervention and ablation results concern selected neurons and limited prompts or contexts, rather than a broad neuron audit. Figure 5 and Figure 7 values are not stated numerically in the text. The paper notes that features may be distributed in superposition and that individual neurons may be the wrong level of analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were retained: the reported neuron measurements and interventions do not measure the versions’ specified audit shares or explanation tests.

untested.parts: All parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares.
All parts: shares across models and scales. The Llama-2/Pythia work here is probing only.
All parts: InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons and recursive generalization.
All parts: architecture, regularization or tools as the cause of messy neurons.
All parts: whether activating-example explanations predict firing.

record.verdict_notes: The study is relevant only as background. It reports neuron-level interpretability for cherry-picked neurons and voices a pro-superposition expectation, but measures nothing on any version. The Table 7 values appear misplaced in the text extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job shares and the proportion not understood.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and the proposed vision-model estimates.
Attribution graphs, behavioral explanation, and comparison with a trained replacement model and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict other firing examples.
Automated explanation scores on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Projected entity activations onto weights of neurons selected for high cosine similarity to learned space/time probe directions; reported Spearman correlations with coordinates.

conditions.value: most similar neurons selected for space/time
space and time datasets; breakdowns by entity type

rows.measure: Spearman correlation between neuron projections and true space or time coordinates
rows.value: Figure 5; the text describes the neurons as highly sensitive to the true coordinates and says they are sensitive across entity types.
rows.note: The main text gives a qualitative description; precise plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Neurons were selected by cosine similarity to probe directions, so this is a selection-dependent case result, not an audit share. Values exist only in Figure 5. The study does not state how many neurons were examined.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b
rows.operation_detail: Pinned the activation of time neuron L19.3610 over a range of values on all tokens and measured next-token probabilities.

conditions.value: one prompt each for a famous song, movie, and book, with a decade completion

rows.measure: Change in top-five next-token predictions as pinned activation varied
rows.value: The text says adjusting this neuron changed the next-token prediction in all cases; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.note: The figure also compares nine random neurons in the same layer; precise values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Single-neuron steering (L19.3610; correlation with release date 0.77 per Appendix B) is compared with 9 random neurons. It reports no rate of interpretability. Values are figure-only.
